g.text: The case conference is in nine days. Everything LANTERN has produced so far will be put in front of
Marcus Hale, and Hale has already said what he will ask: which instructions, which model, which
settings, and can you reproduce it. A demonstration answers none of that. A demonstration is the one run
that happened to work. Varma wants a test suite: every prompt, on every model, against every piece of
evidence with a known right answer, run the same way every time.
. The suite is a config file
description: "Case File 01: can LANTERN's prompts be trusted in court?"
prompts x providers x tests: each test names the prompts it applies to.
. Tests are generated from the evidence
Expected totals come from the seized ledger, case/ledger.csv: the record we must verify.
--reuse: showing the last run instead of running the eval again.
Running 70 test cases (up to 1 at a time)...
Grouping model-graded assertions by provider to minimize local-model reload overhead.
means the run finished and some tests failed. That is a result, not a crash.
. The matrix: pass rate per model and prompt
Open the full results with `make eval-view`
The suite runs end to end and every result is stored with its prompt, model, settings and output. Hale
can have all of it. The rules hold on both models. Extraction is nearly perfect. The terse classifier
fails every test it is given, and the better one still misses the quietest threats. And one extraction
test fails on both models in exactly the same way.
Varma looks at the matrix for a long time. "Before you fix anything, find out what is failing. A failing
